ⓐ.summary: Women will display greater creativity in environments where they work separately from men rather than together with men.

c1.text: Women receive relatively fewer opportunities and lower evaluations compared to men in male-dominated workplaces, regardless of actual ability.

c2.text: If women's opportunities to demonstrate creativity are restricted or their expressions are undervalued in team activities, they cannot fully realize their creative capabilities.

c3.text: ⓐ Women will display greater creativity in environments where they work separately from men rather than environments where they work together with men.

c4.text: In the control group, female singers recorded together with male singers and male musicians; in the experimental group, female singers recorded separately from them.

c5.text: An expert panel evaluated the creative expression of male and female singers by scoring them.

h1.text: The female singers’ scores were higher in the experimental group than in the control group.

a.note: Female singers scoring higher in the experimental group than in the control group shows greater creativity when working separately, supporting ⓐ.

h2.text: The total score of all female singers was higher than that of all male singers.

h3.text: A higher total female score aggregates both groups and could be driven by better performance when collaborating with men, so it does not establish greater creativity when working separately.

b.note: Naive inference rb1 (total female score is higher, so ⓐ is supported) is undercut by h3: total score aggregates both groups and could be driven by higher scores in the control group.

h4.text: In the control group, female singers’ scores were slightly lower than male singers’, but in the experimental group, female singers’ scores were higher than male singers’.

h5.text: Male singers’ scores in the control and experimental groups were comparable.

h6.text: Female singers’ scores were higher in the experimental group than in the control group.

c.note: Assuming comparable male scores across groups, female scores were higher in the experimental group than in the control group, which supports ⓐ rather than weakening it.
